## Server

### Added
- World backups: back up the running world, download a backup, restore one, or upload a save from your own game. A restore or upload backs up the running world first and restarts the server to load the new one. The world it replaced is kept in `lodestone/world-import/replaced/` in the server's files.
- An uploaded world runs under the server's World Name, whatever it was called in your own game.
- The server console says in one line when a world was replaced, and where the old one went.

### Fixed
- The server console opened with the previous start's last error lines. It now opens at this start's first line.
- A world that began on the demo makes the game log a few error lines about areas the demo never had. Beside the demo-world notice they now read as one plain line saying they are expected, instead of red lines with nothing beside them.
- The boot report's world file line names the file the game really holds, not a file built from the world's inner name.

## Client

### Added
- New characters are made on Delverium's own Create Character screen. When your character doesn't exist yet, the game opens Create Character with the name filled in. Choose hair, colours, body, voice and death penalty, press Confirm, and the join carries on. Closing the screen stops the join and makes no character.
- While Create Character is open, the app tells you so, and it remembers the character you made for that server under the name you confirmed.
- The World window has Back up now, and Choose a world picks a world's `.wsv` straight from your own saves (it opens in your World folder). Server replies show in the server's own words, and a server too old for backups says so.
